演奏鑼時，依類型將平盤鑼以繩穿過近上緣孔垂直懸掛，凸心鑼多水平懸掛，碗形鑼置於墊: To play a gong, hang a flat gong vertically by a cord through holes near its upper edge, hang a bossed gong mostly horizontally, and set a bowl gong on a pad. Sound comes from a beater: large gongs take a larger, softer beater, and small hanging gongs can be struck with a bamboo stick or a drumstick. A beginner first masters the striking point and the force; on a large flat gong a light stroke can precede the main stroke so that the sound arrives sooner, but the preliminary stroke must be kept from being heard.

鑼以金屬製成，主要為青銅或黃銅，亦使用多種其他合金；中國銅鑼即因銅合金而得名。c: Gongs are made of metal, mainly bronze or brass, and various other alloys are used too; the Chinese copper gong takes its name from its copper alloy. The chau gong is made of a copper-based alloy, bronze or brass, and the Japanese dora of bronze, brass or iron. The central boss of a bossed gong is often made of a different metal. There are also stone gongs, in which a large stone is struck with a small one. Beaters may be bamboo sticks, Western drumsticks, or tools of wood, plastic or metal; the source does not state the material of the hanging cord.
鑼廣泛見於東南亞與東亞音樂傳統，可獨奏或成組演奏。在西方交響樂團打擊樂部，平鑼（: The gong is widely found in the musical traditions of Southeast Asia and East Asia and can be played solo or in groups. In the percussion section of the Western orchestra the flat gong, or tam-tam, entered orchestral music at the end of the eighteenth century and is used in works by Berlioz, in Wagner's Rienzi and in Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring. In the Indonesian gamelan, gongs of different sizes have different functions and names; in Philippine kulintang music the gong carries the melody. Chinese opera ensembles use pairs of large and small gongs, marking entrances and points in the plot; gongs are also used in Japanese hayashi music, kabuki music, Buddhist ritual and as a signal when a ship leaves port.
鑼為定音體鳴打擊樂器，H-S編號111.241，屬鑼鐘木琴石琴系統。它以金屬製成: The gong is a tuned idiophone of the percussion class, H-S 111.241, in the system of gongs, bells, xylophones and lithophones. It is made of metal, flat, bossed or bowl-shaped, usually struck with a beater, and it can be played solo or in groups. The tradition is widespread in Southeast Asia and East Asia: in China the gong is used in opera and temple ritual, and in Japan in Buddhist services, kabuki and signals for departure.
鑼的起源可追溯至東南亞，最早可能見於北越東山文化玉魯一號青銅鼓（約公元前3至2世: The gong goes back to Southeast Asia, and the earliest evidence may be the image of a seven-gong ensemble on the bronze drum Ngoc Lu 1 of the Dong Son culture of northern Vietnam, around the third to second century BC. Chinese documents mention the gong by the sixth century AD, recording it as a foreign instrument from between Tibet and Burma; the name 'gong' comes from Java in Indonesia. The main centres of manufacture in the past included Annam, Java, Burma and southern China. The gong reached the West in the eighteenth century, was introduced into the orchestra by Gossec in 1790, and later composers such as Stravinsky extended its playing techniques; it has become a member of the orchestral percussion section.
鑼的音色依形制而異：平面懸掛鑼以多模態振動產生無固定音高的撞擊聲；體積越大，通常: The timbre of a gong depends on its form: a flat hanging gong vibrates in many modes and gives a blow without a definite pitch; the larger the instrument, the larger and softer the beater, and a large flat gong can be struck lightly before the main blow so that the sound forms earlier. A bossed gong has a more definite pitch, striking the centre or the edge gives two different timbres, and it shimmers less; some gamelan bossed gongs are deliberately made to beat at about 1 to 5 hertz. A set of tuned bossed gongs can play a melody. In Chinese tradition the large gong is sonorous and strong with a wide range of force, the small gong is crisp, the yunluo has a scale, and the ten-face gong combines several faces of different pitch and timbre; in opera the pitch of a large gong falls and that of a small one rises.
